messages:
carla_support: customer ticket #3456 — large document generation (20k tokens) keeps aborting mid-stream with `ReadTimeout: socket timed out`. They see one successful partial stream, then 1-2 quick retry errors and a duplicate charge. Happened on Dedicated, region us-west-2.

mike_infra: thanks — can you paste their SDK version + how they configure timeouts? also any small repro would help.

carla_support: they say python sdk 0.11.2, server 1.2.0, and they set REDWOOD_TIMEOUT=30 in env and also call Client(timeout=30). error log attached (snippet):
```
ReadTimeout: socket timed out after 30s
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "app.py", line 78, in stream
    for chunk in client.chat.stream(...):
  File "redwood/client/stream.py", line 203, in __iter__
    raise ReadTimeoutError
```

sophie_devx: quick note — in our Python SDK the `timeout` argument maps to requests-style (connect, read) when given as a tuple, but a single int sets the per-chunk read timeout for streaming. env var REDWOOD_TIMEOUT also parsed as int and used as per-chunk timeout in v0.11.2. that explains 30s cutoffs during long gens.

carla_support: they also pasted a tiny repro they run locally:
```
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key="x", timeout=30)
for chunk in c.chat.stream(model="rw-large", prompt="<~20k tokens>"):
    print(chunk.text)
```

mike_infra: ok repro is clear. two things: (1) streaming long generations regularly take >30s between chunks, so per-chunk read timeout should be increased; (2) there was a bug in 0.11.2 where env var + arg parsing interacted and could overwrite tuple timeouts.

sophie_devx: recommended immediate workaround: set explicit tuple timeout so connect vs read are separated, e.g. `Client(timeout=(10, 600))` which sets 10s connect, 600s read. alternatively set `REDWOOD_TIMEOUT` to a larger value (600). For customers that must stream, call streaming with a higher read timeout or disable per-chunk timeout (set to None) until they upgrade.

mike_infra: patch note — we pushed a small fix in 0.11.3 that makes env var parsing consistent and prevents single-int-per-chunk semantics from being silently applied when user intended tuple behavior. strongly recommend upgrade to 0.11.3+.

carla_support: relayed to customer. they asked about duplicate charges on retries — is there guidance?

eng_sre: retries by the SDK default to idempotent-only. Long streaming endpoints are non-idempotent; if the SDK retries after a timeout it can cause a re-run. For now: (a) set retries=0 for stream calls, or (b) set read timeout higher so the SDK doesn't retry mid-generation, and (c) we will add a server-side dedupe header for idempotency in the next minor release.

carla_support: customer upgraded to 0.11.3 locally and set `Client(timeout=(10,900), retries=0)` and reported success — long generation completed and no duplicate billing. marking as resolved. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: deployment 1.2.1 -> canary rolled to us-west-2 (patched env parsing bug)

mike_infra: filing internal follow-ups: (1) add doc note in /docs/sdk/python/timeouts about streaming vs per-chunk; (2) add an FAQ entry about retries + streaming duplication; (3) create unit test to cover REDWOOD_TIMEOUT precedence.

carla_support: thanks all, closing thread.
